candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: handle biohazardous materials safely, protect from injury, and provide safety/infection-prevention teaching.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — home sharps disposal
candidate.educational_objective: Teach home users to place used needles immediately into an appropriate sharps container and dispose of the filled container according to local/community requirements.

options.A: Recap used needles with two hands and then place them loose in household trash after verifying that each cap is secure.
options.B: Flush used needles down the toilet after injection so household members and sanitation workers cannot contact the sharps.
options.C: Keep used needles on an uncovered rigid tray until several have accumulated, then transfer the group into household trash.
options.D: Place each used needle promptly into an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container when available and follow local disposal requirements when the container is ready for removal.

candidate.rationale: FDA recommends placing used needles and other sharps in a sharps disposal container immediately after use. FDA-cleared containers are preferred when available, and when the container is about three-quarters full, community guidelines should be followed for disposal. Loose sharps should not be placed in household/public trash or flushed down the toilet. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Used home injection needles should be placed immediately into an appropriate sharps disposal container, preferably FDA-cleared when available, and the container should be disposed of according to local/community requirements.
candidate.source_document_title: Best Way to Get Rid of Used Needles and Other Sharps
candidate.source_locator: Step 1: place all needles and other sharps in a sharps disposal container immediately after use. Step 2: dispose of used sharps containers according to community guidelines. FDA Sharps Disposal Containers page: FDA-cleared containers are recommended; appropriate heavy-duty household containers may be alternatives when cleared containers are unavailable.
candidate.source_version_date: Current FDA consumer guidance; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A client self-administers insulin at home. Which instruction about used needles is appropriate?
